title: Ai Khanoum (Hellenistic city on the Oxus)
summary: Ai Khanoum is a ruined Hellenistic city in northern Afghanistan, on a plain between the Amu Darya (Oxus) and Kokcha rivers. Thought to have been founded around 300 BC, it had a palace, a gymnasium and temples whose plans blended Greek and Central Asian forms. A palace fire around 145 BC marked the end of the Greek city; French excavations ran from 1964 to 1978.

uncertainty.note: Start is "around 300 BC" (The Past) = astronomical -299; World History Encyclopedia says only "4th century BC". End is the palace burning "around 145 BC" (-144); WHE says the Sakas took the town "between 145 and 138 BC".

reviewer_note: Least sure of the founding date: the two sources disagree (4th century BC vs around 300 BC), so the range is wide. The Past does not state excavation years in its text; the 1964-1978 span is from World History Encyclopedia. Identification with Alexandria on the Oxus was not stated on an opened page and is not claimed. Pin is the Wikidata point for the site.
